component: P1.1 core package checker: compared artifact, installer and report binding
constraints: Offline Python wheel consumer; retain the exact compared bytes through pip installation and evidence output; no new runtime dependency or measured hard-real-time requirement.
comparison: Python hashlib.sha256 hashes the already-compared immutable bytes directly. RustCrypto sha2 can implement the same digest through a native boundary; external hash tools can hash files but require another read unless explicitly supplied the retained bytes. Neither alternative removes the existing Python/pip installation boundary.
rationale: KEEP Python orchestration with its native-backed stdlib hashlib for this narrow observer: same-buffer hashing and hash-enforced pip admission provide the required binding without an additional serialization, subprocess or FFI boundary. No throughput comparison or global language preference is claimed.
evidence: Three mutation subcases failed before the correction. The checker now captures compared bytes once, pins pip with a SHA-256 file URL plus --require-hashes/--force-reinstall, and reports that retained digest. Tests cover changes after comparison read, before install and after install, including URI-escaped spaces and #.

Ten focused core package methods passed. Separate real pip controls installed a harmless synthetic wheel with its correct hash and rejected an incorrect hash before installation. Product consumers are mocked in regression tests; no product runtime was executed.
limits: source_sha256 binds the pre-correction observer at source_revision. Tests and updated observer accompany this decision. A matching hash authenticates the compared artifact, not its publisher or source tree.

This does not establish source-tree immutability, installed-file tamper resistance, CLI wrapper coverage, cross-platform release qualification or completion of P1.1-P1.7. Existing dependency_installation=false means --no-deps, not inspected absence of dependency metadata.
revisit: Continue P1.1 installed CLI/source binding review, including synthetic backend observers; qualify actual consumers on the exact delivery head before release.
